Severe Flooding Impacts Engineering & Construction Sites in Southern Brazil

Heavy rainfall over the past week has triggered severe flooding across the state of Santa Catarina, causing widespread disruption to the Engineering & Construction industry’s operational sites. The ongoing deluge, which began Sunday night, has inundated several construction plants and project sites in the greater Joinville and Blumenau regions, forcing partial shutdowns and placing hundreds of workers at risk.

According to the Santa Catarina Engineering & Construction Association (SCECA), at least 11 major construction sites operated by local and national firms have been affected. “The volume of rain is unprecedented for this time of year and has resulted in extensive waterlogging at our ongoing infrastructure and building projects,” said SCECA president Luiz Henrique da Silva. “Foundations have been compromised and equipment damaged. In some locations, work has ground to a halt as safety cannot be guaranteed.”

Several prefabrication yards and material storage facilities, particularly those along the Itajaí-Açu River, have also reported flooding, with managers racing to relocate valuable stock and machinery to higher ground. At Construtora Nova Horizonte’s site near Gaspar, water levels rose by over 1.5 meters, submerging precast concrete modules and damaging electrical panels. Company spokesperson Maria Fernanda Tavares described the situation as “critical,” noting that more than 60 workers were evacuated as a precaution.

Site engineers across the region are monitoring slope stability at hillside projects, as saturated soil raises the risk of landslides. “We are prioritizing worker safety and have suspended activities at all affected sites,” said João Pedro Matos, operations manager at EngenhoSul. “The extent of structural damage will only become clear once the water recedes.”

Union representatives have called for emergency support for impacted employees. “Many site workers have lost access to safe working conditions and are facing uncertainty about their livelihoods,” said Paulo Azevedo, regional coordinator for the Construction Workers’ Union.

With meteorologists warning of continued rainfall in the coming days, industry leaders are bracing for further disruptions and urging all firms to remain vigilant. The full impact on ongoing projects across Santa Catarina’s Engineering & Construction sector will be assessed as conditions evolve.
